correctness.rationale: Actual cyclic edges close and yield six facet supports. Writing z=(1+λ)o turns reflected homothety containment into three paired intervals for zx,zy,zx+zy. Their sum intervals intersect iff λ(S+t)≥S and λS≥S+t. At λ*=max(T/S,S/T), upper or lower coordinate boundaries become jointly active and force the given unique optimizer even for t=0. Positivity bounds s<2; a=c=ε,b=1,t=(r−1)(1+2ε) realizes every 1<r<2, t=0 realizes 1. Independently checked all six rational inequalities for positive, negative and zero t using exact Fractions.
residual_risks: The proof is specifically for six positive edges in three paired directions; its finite rational checks do not establish universality without the interval argument.

value.rationale: This computes a natural and affine-invariant asymmetry and rigid critical point for the complete first nontrivial class of paired-parallel-edge hexagons, including nonsymmetric examples. The entire four-parameter shape family collapses to one ratio, with a sharp geometric range; it is neither a mere named substitution nor arbitrary numerical sampling.
residual_risks: No analogous classification is asserted for all even-gons or 3D bodies.

final_claim: For every strictly convex six-edge polygon with parallel opposite sides, the affine-normalized positive edge parameters a,b,c,a+t,b-t,c+t give Minkowski asymmetry max((S+t)/S,S/(S+t)), S=a+b+c, a unique optimal center and sharp range [1,2).
limitations: Finite numerical checker is supplemental; six-facet interval proof supplies universality.
